title: A paragraph header whose separator period is on the next line
shapes: 1100-OPEN-MSG alone on its line, the separator period alone on the next (GLPOST)
asserts: 1100-OPEN-MSG is a paragraph from its name to its last code line.

citations.doc: Enterprise COBOL for z/OS 6.4 Language Reference (SC27-8713-03)
citations.quote: A space can immediately precede or follow any separator except: The opening pseudo-text delimiter ... Within quotation marks.

citations.doc: Enterprise COBOL for z/OS 6.4 Language Reference (SC27-8713-03)
citations.quote: If there is no hyphen (-) in the indicator area (column 7) of a line, the last character of the preceding line is assumed to be followed by a space.

lower_confidence: No IBM sentence states outright that a paragraph-name's separator period may be on the next line; it follows from the separator and continuation rules (an end of line is a space; a space may precede a separator period). GnuCOBOL -std=ibm accepts it.
